title: Statistical Analysis
text:
Welcome






Scaffold edition



The chapter structure is ready. Method chapters are outlines awaiting worked examples and statistical review.


Use this free CDI reference to move from a question to an analysis you can explain and defend.

Start with Questions and methods.
Review Statistical inference.
Try the runnable two-group example.
Apply your learning in the Statistical Inference Practical.

Your question → Your inputs → Run the analysis → Check evidence → Explain with limitations.
Examples will use R and Python as appropriate. Bash scripts handle setup and workflow checks.

title: Preface
text:
How each chapter works
This guide is a reference: read the foundations once, then open the chapter that matches your question and design.
Question, suitable use, target estimate or hypothesis, assumptions, runnable analysis, output interpretation, reporting, and alternatives.

title: Preface
text:
Current status
This is a scaffold, not a finished statistical textbook. Chapter 05 includes a runnable starter example. Other chapters contain explicit development prompts.

title: Preface
text:
Tools
Use R or Python for analysis and Bash for setup and checks. Run commands from the repository root. Rendering does not run the external analysis scripts; run them separately when developing examples.
See README.md for setup. The examples use synthetic data and do not establish real-world effects.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Your question
What is the mean difference in scores between independent groups B and A?

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
When to use this method
The outcome is numerical and the groups contain different participants. Welch’s t-test allows unequal population variances. It does not correct dependence, selection bias, or confounding.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
What it estimates or tests
The effect is the population mean of B minus the population mean of A. The two-sided null hypothesis is a zero mean difference.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Check before running
Check the study design, group counts, missing data, and distributions. Inspect extreme observations. With small samples, strong skew or outliers can undermine the t approximation.
The example file has one row per synthetic participant. Its independence is part of how the example was generated.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Run the analysis
From the project root, choose either implementation:
python3 scripts/python/05-independent-t-test.py
Rscript scripts/R/05-independent-t-test.R
Both use data/example/independent-groups.csv, calculate B minus A, and export separate TSV results under results/tables/.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Understand the output
Read the mean difference and its 95% confidence interval together. The interval expresses uncertainty under the model and sampling assumptions. The p-value measures incompatibility with the zero-difference null under those assumptions; it does not measure practical importance.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Report the finding
Report sample sizes, group means, the B-minus-A difference, its confidence interval, Welch’s t statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value. These synthetic scores illustrate a method and support no claim about a real intervention.

title: Independent-Samples t-Test
text:
Common mistakes and alternatives
Do not use an independent-groups test for paired measurements. Do not select tests solely from a normality-test p-value. Rank tests answer a different question and are not automatic tests of medians.
